memebrs’ accounts, in continuation of the arrangements made in the previous months, the
Officers-incharge have now been empowered to allot the work of settlement of claims to APFCs
and updation of members’ acocunts to AOs on need basis, apart from their regular duties.
Similarly, Section Supervisors have also been empowered to settle claims upto a monetary
ceiling of ¥ 25,000/-, thus bringing the settlement process from three levels to two levels.

revision after 24" of the month. Similarly the claim Form 10C, 10D, 5IF & 31 may be settled
between 25" to 31% of this month. The above advice is only to ensure that all the claims are
settled by 31% March 2012.

Sub: Work Order for providing Wide Area Network (WAN) for EPFO using MPLS VPN
Connectivity — Regarding.
Ref: Your proposal for WAN Solution for EPFO Dated 21/02/2012.
Sir,

With reference to your proposal cited, | am pleased to convey acceptance of your
proposal mentioned above for providing Wide Area Network (WAN) to EPFO using MPLS VPN
Connectivity.

The WAN connectivity for EPFO is required for implementing the Integrated Challan &
Return (ICR) Project of EPFO and strict deadlines have to be met. We would request you to
commence work on the implementation of the WAN immediately to ensure time bound
completion of the work.

The list of 20 EPFO locations where 1 Mbps connections, 100 EPFO Locations where 512
Kbps connections, 2 locations where 10 Mbps and one location where 100 Mbps Internet
Connections are to be established are given at Annexure A.

The broad terms and conditions of the work orders are as under:

1. Annual bandwidth charges for all the links mentioned in the proposal shall be
Rs.3,23,48,700/- (Rupees Three Crore Twenty Three Lakh Forty Eight Thousand Seven
Hundred Only). Taxes as per actuals will be extra and payable by EPFO. The annual
bandwidth charges may undergo change in case of addition of site on pro-rata basis and
on change of bandwidth at the mutually agreed rates.

2. The MPLS-VPN WAN Network for EPFO will be hired with acommitment period of two
years. EPFO may further extend the order as per requirement.

offices as per the proposal by 31/03/2012 and made operational. In the event that if
not possible to implement the same at certain site, BSNL shall furnish list of locations
and the expected date of implementation for each site of EPFO.

4. Billing will commence from 01/05/2012. For pending sites getting commissioned after
the billing period date, billing shall start as per actual date of commissioning site wise.

5. Any MPLS connections which are not commissioned beyond May 2012 will not be billed
till its actual commissioning site wise.

6. Routers (CISCO make} and modems will be provided by BSNL as part of bandwidth.

7. The MPLS-VPN of EPFO will be configured and managed by BSNL. BSNL will also provide
24 X 7 support for complaints and fault resolution.

8. BSNL will ensure 99.5% uptime (monthly basis} and 150 ms or better latency for the
network for individual links.

The broad terms and conditions mentioned above along with other terms and service
level assurances will be contained in the Service Level Agreement (SLA) to be entered into
between EPFO & BSNL.

Sub: Empanelment of visiting Faculty of ZTI (WZ), Ujjain- regarding.

Sir,

As you are aware training is one of the most cost effective and tested tools for improving
employee productivity. National training policy of Govt. of India has accordingly emphasized the
importance of training function in Government. In a service organization like EPFO training
assumes added significance.

ZTI, WZ, caters to the training needs of Gr.’B’, ‘C’ & ‘D’ staff posted in 11 Regions and at
an average the institute runs 59 training courses in a year. Multipronged measures are being
taken to improve the effectiveness of the training programmes by way of improving the training
design, provision of study material and improving the learning environment in the class room
using various training and learning aids.

The institute is, however, facing enormous difficulties in arranging faculty for its various
training courses. There is only one APFC in the institute who looks after the administrative
function as well as training activities. Most of the training sessions are taken by the visiting
faculties. In view of the location of the institute faculties are either drawn from RO Indore or
retired officials residing in Indore. This constraint is seriously affecting the quality of
training programs. In this context, it is felt that situation can be improved by tapping the
pool of competent and willing officers available in various offices of West Zone.

As an important stakeholder, your kind cooperation is solicited for improving the training
and development of staff posted in your region. You are, therefore, requested to kindly forward
the name of the officers who are willing to take training sessions in various training courses in
the next calendar year. The draft training calendar for 2012-13 is enclosed.

Kindly accord priority.
Yours faithfully,
Sd/-

Subject: Delegation of financial powers to the Section Supervisor (SS) for speedy
settlement of claims.

Sir,

Central P.F. Commissioner in exercise of Powers conferred upon him under para 24(3)
of the EPF Scheme, 1952 has approved the delegation of Financial Powers for authorization of
claims upto % 25,000/ by the Section Supervisor (SS) and beyond % 25,000/- by the Accounts
Officer (AO). Accordingly, following changes have been incorporated in the EPFO Application
Software (Version 3.29 dated 03.03.2012) and the same is to be implemented with immediate
effect: -

1. Form-10D (Input Data Sheet) is changed from three levels to two levels where DA
(Accounts) will submit the claim form and it will be approved by AO (Accounts).

2. Form-19, Form-20, Form-20 (Special), Form-13 (Un-exempted), Form-14 (LIP
Payment) and Form-31 the following changes are done-:

a. The forms are reduced to two levels from three levels where Claim will be
submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by SS (Claims) in case the
Settlement amount is up to = 25,000/- including inoperative accounts.

b. The forms are reduced to two levels from three levels where Claim will be
submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by AO (Accounts) in case the
Settlement amount is more than = 25000/-.

C. In case setthement of claims out of inoperative accounts, Claim will be
submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by AO (Accounts) in case the
Settlement amount is more than % 25,000/ and less than % 50,000/-.

d. In case settlement of claims out of inoperative accounts, Claim will be
submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by APFC in case the settlement
amount is beyond = 50,000/-. ,

3. Form-13 (Exempted) approval is changed three levels to two levels i.e. DA
(Accounts) to SS (Claims).

4, Form 5-IF and Form 5-IF (Special) is changed from three levels to two levels i.e.
DA (Accounts) to AO (Accounts).

10.

The return/rejection of claims is changed from three levels to two levels in which
DA (Accounts) will submit the return/rejection and AO (Accounts) will approve it.

The broken period 3A where settlement amount is up to % 25,000/-, DA (Accounts)
will submit the 3A and SS claims will approve the same.

The broken period 3A where settlement amount is beyond = 25,000/-, DA
(Accounts) will submit the 3A and AO (Accounts) will approve the same.

In finalization of accounts the changes are as follow:-

3A/6A will be originated by DA and approved by AC.

6A summary approval remains unchanged (i.e. DA/SS/AC).

3A vs. Challan reconciliation remains unchanged (i.e. DA/SS/AC).
IPR (Interest Processing) remains unchanged i.e. DA only.
Form-24 will be generated and approved manually by DA/SS/AC.

Sub:- Representation in Board for Industrial & Financial Reconstruction (BIFR)/Appellate Authority
for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (AAIFR).

Ref:- (i) This Office Circular letter No. C-II/18(2)10/Misc/BIFR/AAIFR/36028 dated 31.01.2011.
(ii) This Office Circular letter No. C-II/28(2)06/BIFR/83364 dated 03.02.2010.
(iii) This Office Circular letter No. LC-2(724)/2011/GJ/17827 dated 16.11.2011.

Sir,

It has been observed that despite issue of instructions vide circular letter dated 03.02.2010 and
31.01.2011, certain field Offices send BIFR/AAIFR cases to Head Office for filing claims and taking follow
up action. In this regard, it is stated that Section 11 of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 gives statutory priority to
the amounts dues from the employer vis-a-vis all other debts and in view of the Supreme Court
Judgements circulated vide letter dated 03.02.2010 and 16.11.2011 cited at (ii) & (iii) above: All such
cases of BIFR/AAIFR are being dealt within the concerned Offices of the EPFO. As such the concerned
Office has to plead his case through one of its Officer whenever required to file claim/documents and
process with BIFR/AAIFR duly incorporating the provisions of EPF & MP Act, 1952 and the Judgements of
Hon’ble Supreme Court of India.

In the light of above facts, it is made clear that you should evolve mechanism for processing the
cases with BIFR/AAIFR without putting responsibility on the Head Office. You may also instruct your
Officers to evince adequate responsibility to keep track of the situation and follow the
guidelines/instructions issued in this Office Circular letter dated 31.01.2011 cited at (i) above.

Sir/Madam,

Please refer to the subject cited above.

This is to inform that the Employees’ P F Organisation was one of the nine
Departments/Organisations to implement Sevottam (Service Delivery Excellence) which included
development of Citizen’s Charter.

Under RFD also the implementation of Sevottam was made a mandatory item and
accordingly the Citizen’s Charter revised as per the guidelines issued by the Department of
Administrative Reforms and Public Grievance along with the Performance Management Division of
the Cabinet Secretariat for the Sevottam Compliant Citizen’s Charter has been approved by the Board
and the Ministry.

As per the guidelines a single page containing extracts of main services and standards from
the charter are to be displayed at the Reception and other prominent places in the Offices.

The Citizen’s Charter in English and Hindi has been uploaded on the epfindia website and the
link is on the home page.

It is therefore request to display the Service Standards listed in the Charter in the Reception
area of your office.

Sir;
Two posts of Vigilance Assistant in the Pay Band-2 of Rs. 9300-34800 with grade
pay of Rs. 4200/- (Scale of pay Rs. 5500-175-9000 ,pre-revised) in respect of the following
zones/ Offices are proposed to be filled up by transfer on deputation basis from amongst

the employees of the Employees’ Provident Fund Orpanization:-

° 2 posts in the Vigilance Head Quarter at Head Office, EPFO, New Delhi.

a Tpost in in the Zonal Vigilance Directorate (West Zone) at Mumbai.

These posts are to be filled up on deputation basis for a period not exceeding three years in
the first instance. The prescribed norms as per Recruitment Rules for the post of Vigilance
Assistant are as follows:-

Qualification :-

“ Transfer on deputation amongst officials of Employees’ Provident Fund
Organisation having experience in Vigilance work and holding analogous post in the pay
scale of Rs. 5500-175-9000 (pre-revised) or three years regular service in the pay scale of

Rs. 5000-150-8000 (pre-revised).”

You are therefore requested to arrange to circulate the above vacancies amongst

the staff members of your Regional and Sub-Regional Offices accordingly, and the
application received from the candidate fulfilling the prescribed requirement as indicated
above may please be forwarded to this office (addressed by name to Sh P K Agarwal [RPFCHRM) along with their detailed service particulars as per enclosed proforma, the
photocapies of the Annual Confidential Reports for the last five years duly attested and the
VCC/IC so as to reach this office not later than 15.03.2012. In case no application is
received by the stipulated time, it will be presumed that there is no application for theses
posts fram your region.

Sub : To fix time line for redressal of grievances.

Sir,

You are aware that online grievances from DARPG are forwarded and monitored through
CPGRAM. The responsibility center for head office and other higher authorities is Regional Office,
as below Regional Office direct monitoring is not done by these authorities.

Ministry of Labour and employment has noted that timely action has not been taken by the
organization for redressal of grievances and the same remain pending for unduly long periods.

The observation of the ministry is correct to some extent as in a number of offices case are
pending even beyond 1-3 years. Customer Service Division Head Office is repeatedly reminding the
RPFC’s through e-mail,post as well as telephonically. Although good no. of grievances have been
redressed during the year still majority of the cases pending belong to the category beyond 6
month - 1 year. A detail list and summery report is send through e-mail from time to time. A latest
report of pending cases is enclosed herewith.

Hence fourth a monthly meeting will be held in the Ministry of Labour on last Friday of the
month . In February it will be held on 24" February 2012.

Please insure that at least the grievance beyond One year are redressed within a week.
Further please design a system of formally reviewing the grievance area by holding meeting fort
nightly or monthly as may be convenient.

Subject: Incentive. to employers in the Private Sector for providing regular
employment to the persons with disabilities regarding.
Sir,

Kind attention is invited to Head Office letter No. Coord./Misc./2007/3907 dated
08.05.2008 on the above subject.

2. The performance on coverage of physically disabled persons under the Scheme
was reviewed in the 7" meeting of the High Level Monitoring Committee held on 23.01.2012 in
the Ministry of Labour & Employment, New Delhi. It was viewed that even though a
considerable amount was granted by Ministry of Social Justice for Publicity of the Scheme, the
enrollment of persons with disabilities by EPFO offices is very poor. While comparing the
enrollment by ESIC and EPFO, it is found that while ESIC has enrolled 652 persons, EPFO
enrolled only 320 persons. Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment has expressed his
displeasure on such poor performance.

3. In order to improve the coverage of persons with disabilities the following
directions are issued for strict compliance:-

(i) The matter may be taken up with DGE&T at Regional / Sub-Regional Level to
arrive at the correct number of persons with disabilities registered with them.

(ii) Regional Vocational Rehabilitation Centres under your jurisdiction may also be
contacted for obtaining data of deployment of persons with disabilities in private
sectors.

(iii) |The exempted establishments under your jurisdiction may also be contacted and
efforts be made to popularise the Scheme for employment of disabled persons
therein.

(iv) |The Non Government Organisations (NGOs) and other Organisations may also be
contacted which are mainly working for upliftment of physically disabled persons
so that they can be educated to popularise the benefits of this Incentive Scheme for
improving the enrolment.

(v) Regular seminars and workshops may be organised with employers’ organisations
to persuade them to employ persons with disabilities and avail the benefits of the
Scheme.

(vi) | Nodal Officers may be nominated in each region for strict compliance of the above
instructions and to furnish the information /data to Head Office. The details of the
Nodal Officer, so nominated at regional level may be sent to Head Office for
further coordination with them.

(vii) The details of coverage under the Incentive Scheme may also be exchanged with
ESIC. The inputs received from ESIC may be thoroughly examined for coverage
under the provision of EPF and MP Act 1952.

4. While enrolling the persons with disabilities, the instructions contained in this
office circular dated 08.05.2008 may be followed. There should not be any repetition of persons
who have already been enrolled under the Scheme and who have completed 3 years on or after
01.04.2008.

5. Immediate Action may be taken on the above lines so that convincing
improvement in the coverage of persons with disabilities could be achieved in a months’ time and
a better report could be placed before the next meeting of the High Level Monitoring Committee
on behalf of EPFO.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Supply of information under Right to Information Act, 2005.

Whereas Sh. V.S. Subramani has made a request in writing vide his application
dated 04.01.2012 for obtaining information under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

2. Whereas the undersigned having been appointed as CPIO under Section 5(1) of

the said Act is required to consider and provide the information within 30 days of the
receipt of the request.

3. And whereas Section 5(4) of the Act provides the CPIO may seek the assistance
of any other officer as he considers it necessary for the proper discharge of his duties.
Sub-section (5) further provides that any officer whose assistance has been sought shall
render all assistance to the CPIO. Once the complaint is referred “for the purposes of any
contravention of the provisions of the Act, such other officer shall be treated as CPIO”
and may be liabie for penalties under Section 20 of the said Act. -Further in the event of
violation of provisions / non-furnishing of documents / information such an officer is liable
for penalties under Section 20(1) of the Act @ Rs. 250/- for each day of the delay which
may extend up to Rs. 25,000/-.

4. And whereas under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act it has been provided that :

“where an application is made to a public authority requesting for an information :-
(i) which is held by another public authority, or

(ii) the subject matter of which is more closely connected with the functions of
another public authority,

the public authority, to which such application is made, shall transfer the application or
such part of it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the
applicant immediately about such transfer”.

5. Whereas on scrutiny of the application, I find that the information sought by the
applicant at point No. (1), (2) & (3) is closely related to and held by CPIOs of the
Regions / Sub-Regional Offices, the undersigned invokes the provisions of Section
5(4) of the said Act and transfér the application to furnish the information / documents
sought by the applicant under the RTI Act, 2005 within the prescribed time limit directly
to the applicant. You may please note that any delay in furnishing the information /
documents sought for within the stipulated time limit will attract the penal provisions as
provided for under Section 20 of the RTI Act.

6. This may please be treated as MOST URGENT.

Sir,

Please refer to Head Office letter No. HRD/4(1)2009/Misc./Circular/10359 dated
26'" May 2009 through which the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme
(MACPS) issued by Department of Personnel and Training vide letter No.
35034/3/2008-Estt. (D) dated 19.05.2009 was circulated.

There in it had been mentioned that cases for grant of financial upgradations
would be considered by a Screening Committee consisting a Chairperson and two
members. The members of the Committee would be at least one level above the grade
in which MACP is to be considered and not below the rank of Under Secretary
equivalent in the Government. The Chairperson should generally be from a grade
above than the members of the Committee. Thus the members of committee may be
drawn from the grade of RPFC-II or above and the Chairman should be in the rank of
RPFC-I or above.

It has however been observed that many of the Regional Offices have either not

sent their complete proposal for Financial Upgradation under MACPS in respect of Data

Entry Operator who have completed 10/20/30 years service or have forwarded merely

the claim of the concerned official in this regard.

In order to have uniform processing of the claims of officials for benefits under
MACPS, RPFCs-I in-charge of the Region are requested that all the cases, coming
within the zone of consideration for MACPS benefits, be considered by the Screening
Committee constituted in the region in accordance with above cited DOPT Circular.
Recommendations of the Screening Committee alongwith supporting documents i.e.
Service Particulars in detail (from date of joining onwords) subsequent
promotions/financial upgradations, ACR Gradings, Vigilance Clearance Certificate etc.
may be forwarded to the Head Office through proper channel for their processing and

related action.

So far as the pending cases coming under the erstwhile ACP Scheme (i.e. for
benefits as per their eligibility upto 31.08.2008) are concerned they may be identified
and be referred to Head Office in accordance with the guidelines issued vide this office
Circular No. P.1V/3(2)/99/5707 dated 22.10.99 and No.
HRD/4(1)2010/Misc./Circular/Pt.1/12145, dated 25.1.2011.

Please acknowledge and inform the action taken in this regard.

Yours faithfully,

(P K AGARWAL)

1.Leave granted.




2. The question which falls for consideration before
this Court in this case is whether the employer of
an establishment which is an `exempted
establishment' under the Employees' Provident Funds
and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (hereinafter,
`the Act') is subject to the provisions of Section
14B of the said Act whereby in cases of default in
the payment of contribution to the provident fund,
proceedings for recovery of damages can be initiated
3

against the employer of such an `exempted
establishment'.

High Court and both the Single Bench and the
Division Bench of the High Court have recorded a
finding in favour of the respondent and held that
the respondent being an `exempted establishment'
cannot be subjected to the provisions of Section
14(B) of the Act.




4.The material facts of case are not much in dispute.

Sir,
Due to
various
reasons, a
large
number
of
claims
for
settlement
of
members'
dues/withdrawals/accounts have accumulated in different offices during the current year.
In
addition, updation of accounts for the year 2010-11 has also been pending for the same reasons in
these offices. Instructions have been issuedto all the field offices with a view to acceleratethe pace
of settlement of claims and updation of all pending members' accounts so that there is no backlog in
these areas except claims received within 30 days. Last such instruction was issuedon 16th January,
2012, particularly, to those offices which had huge backlogs.
2.
In order to expedite this process and achieve the desired result, all the offices have been
permitted to engage as many Data Entry Operators from outside on contract basis as needed
irrespective of number of vacancies in their respective offices to augment the shortage of manpower
to the possible extent. Further, procedure for settling the claims have been Simplified vide this office
letter No.WSU/1O(1)2011/changes in MAP/44489 dated 18.1.2012 with a view to expedite the
process. With these steps it is estimated that most of the offices would be able to achieve the target
of liquidating the pending claims and updation of members' accounts including for the year 2010-11
by 31st March, 2012.
However, this would require concerted efforts,
close monitoring and
supervision by the concerned ROs/SROs.
3.

achieve the above target by the steps already initiated, however, some of them particularly those
where pendency is very large, they would require their staff to work beyond office hours as well as
on holidays to achieve the target of liquidating all the pending cases excluding those which are
received within 30 days along with the updation of pending accounts by 31st March, 2012. It has

as well as on holidays, but also achieve certain minimum level of productivity

Subject: Fraudulent withdrawals from the Accounts of EPFO through fake chequesinstructions to avoid fraudulent payment- reg.

Sir,

In order to avoid fraudulent withdrawals due to tampering of cheques and to mitigate
undue hardship to the PF beneficiaries in getting their Provident Fund accumulations, instructions
were issued vide this office circular Nos. (1) Bkg/Fraud/05/18210 dated 22/11/2011, posted at SI.
No. 405 and (2) Bkg/Fraud/05/15614 dated 24/11/2011, posted at SI. No. 408 of the official
website of the organization under Office Orders & Circulars for the year 2011-12.

2. Inspite of the said instructions, the following issues could not be resolved :

a) There is-no facility provided in the Application Software for remitting
provident fund monies in death cases (Form-20) through NEFT.

b) There is no facility provided in the Application Software for remitting
provident fund monies to the Exempted Trusts through NEFT.

c) Payment of provident fund monies(Form-19} beyond Rs. 1,00,000/-
through NEFT are not possible in the cases where the members

maintain accounts with Co-operative Banks, Regional Rural Banks and
Post Offices.

d) Pension payments going through BRS involves amount beyond the limit
of Rs. 50,000/- and there is no provision in the Application Software for
remitting the same through NEFT.

3. To resolve the above issues, the following instructions were issued vide this office circular
No. Bkg/Fraud/05/39906 dated: 20.12.2011 posted at SI. No. 460 of the official website of the
organization under Office Orders & Circulars for the year 2011-12:

Page 1 of 2

a) Payment to Exempted Trusts on account of transfer(Form-13) may be made
through Account Payee Demand Draft/Bankers’ Cheque.

b) Payment of Provident Fund to members, in case of Form-19/nominees of the
deceased members in case of Form-20 where amount involved is more than
Rs. 1,00,000/- and where bank accounts of the member/nominees of the
member are in Co-operative Banks and Regional Rural Banks, may be made
through Account Payee Demand Draft/Bankers’ Cheque.

4. Now, the Information Services Division has made further Provisions in the Application
Software so that the payments in the cases, cited at Para 3 above, can be made through National
Electronic Fund Transfer(NEFT) except in cases where bank accounts of the member/nominees of
the member are in Co-operative Banks and Regional Rural Banks. There is no need to incorporate
the bank branch addresses in all claims for NEFT payment. However, verification of IFSC Code,
Account Number, Bank and Bank Branch name should invariably be carried out from cancelled
cheque/photocopy of bank passbook enclosed along with the Claim Form. All these have been taken
care of in the War version 3.2 to all offices issued by IS Division. But payment on account of Form
5(IF) through NEFT has been deferred due to major change in the Application Software.

5. The payment of Provident Fund to members, in case of Form-19/nominees of the deceased
members in case of Form-20, where bank accounts of the member/nominees of the member are in
Co-operative Banks and Regional Rural Banks and amounts involved is upto Rs. 1,00,000/-, shall
continue to be paid through cheques. But payment beyond Rs. 1,00,000/-,in such cases, shall
continue to be made through Account Payee Demand Draft/Bankers’ Cheque.

6. The Payment of Pension through designated Banks shall continue to be governed by
instructions contained in this office circular No. Bkg/Fraud/05/39906 dated: 20.12.2011 posted at

SI. No. 460 of the official website of the organization under Office Orders & Circulars for the year
2011-12.

Yours faithfully,

Sir,

Reference may be made to above referred letters.

Various instructions from Head office emphasizing the importance of proper monitoring
of court cases and taking appropriate action for defending them have been issued from time to
time, especially in the recent past. It is presumed that monthly and quarterly reviews are being
conducted to watch the development of the cases as well as performance of the panel counsels.

However, from perusal of the reports being received from the Zonal ACCs, it appears
that still there are many cases where counter affidavit/reply and/or stay vacating applications
are not filed inspite of lapse of more than a year. The stereotype reasons for this position like
letters written to advocate are not acceptable and it is advised to take concrete action so that
counter affidavits are filed and stay is vacated and pending cases are disposed off by courts at
an early date.

Further in view of the present panel of advocates which was constituted for the
block year 2011-2012 and Zonal ACCs having been delegated to reconstitute the panel, the
process for recasting the panel for 2012-2014 may be initiated after evaluating the
performance of existing panel advocates and introduction of new ones as per requirement and
number of cases.It is once again reiterated that ineffective advocate may not be allowed to
continue..

Yours faithfully,

Sir,
References have been received from some Regional Offices with regards to the
fixation of pay in the cadre of Social Security Assistants (SSAs) who are drawing the
pay scale of Rs.5200-20200 in PB-1 with Grade Pay of Rs.2400/- [Rs.4000-100-600 .0
(pre-revised)] on completion of 4 years of regular service and their placement in the
time scale of Rs.5200-20200 in PB-1 with Grade Pay of Rs.2800/- [Rs.4500-125-7000
(pre-revised)].
In this regard, it is stated that the Head Office vide OM No. HRD/1(9)2003/Pay
Scales/Pt-11/60951 dated 14/15 November 2007(copy enclosed) has clarified the
fixation of pay of SSAs on their placement in the time scale on completion of 4 years of
regular service. The Para 3 of this OM has clarified the method of fixation of pay which
reads as under:-
"The fixation of pay in the revised scale shall be done under FR 22(1)(a)(2)
except in the case of Sr. SSA. Fixation on promotion to the grade as Sr. SSA will
however be made under FR 22(1)(a)(1), as a special case".
Hence, it is again reiterated that fixation of pay of SSAs who are drawing the
pay scale of Rs.5200-20200 in PB-1 with Grade Pay of Rs.2400/- [Rs.4000-100-6000
(pre-revised)] on completion of 4 years 'of regular service and their placement in the
time scale of Rs.5200-20200 in PB-1 with Grade Pay of Rs.2800/- [Rs.4500-125-7000
(pre-revised)] shall be done strictly in accordance with Head Office OM No.
HRD/1(9)2003/Pay Scales/Pt-11/60951 dated 14/15 November 2007.

Subject: Deduction of Intercity charges by link branches of field offices- reg.

Sir,

On scrutiny of bank statement of A/c No. V (10996680180) & XI (10996680168), it is
found that link branches of some field offices are deducting Intercity Charges for transfer of fund
from A/c No. I to V / X to XI and vice-versa under NFMS. As per clause 5.19.2(10) of Agreement on
banking arrangement of funds between EPFO and SBI, there will not be any additional charges on
the transfer of daily closing balances by the link branches to SBI Mumbai main Branch or vice-versa.
The matter was taken up with the State Bank of India and SBI has informed that there are inherent
instructions provided in the system of State Bank of India for not debiting bank charges on the
transactions of EPFO. It could be that some link branches have not put such instructions in the
system.

2: In view of above, all the Field Offices are requested to check as to whether the Intercity
charges are being debited from A/c No. I or X by State Bank of India on EPFO transactions and if
the intercity charges are being debited from A/c No. I & X, it should be taken up with the link
branch for updating the instructions in their system for non-debit of any charges on the transactions
of EPFO and for reversal of such charges debited already if any.

Yours faithfully,

Regional P F Commissioner-I

Subject:- Redressal of grievances received from Cabinet
Secretariat, Directorate of Public Grievances- regarding.

Sir,

The grievances from Cabinet Secretariat, DGP are directly sent to
Regional Office depending on the grievances description. In some cases the
grievance is registered against an office to which it really does not pertain to.
There are instructions that any office receives grievances but pertaining to some
other office, it shall follow up with the concerned office, obtain a reply and send
the same to DGP office. In a number of cases various offices have reacted to the
grievances adopting a very narrow approach and simply replying to DGP that
“the case does not pertain to their office”. A meeting was held in DGP on 21th
Dec. 2011 and this approach of field offices indirectly shifting a responsibly to
Cabinet Secretariat to directly follow up with the office, is not appreciated.

Hence, fourth you are strictly requested not to dispose off any case with
the remark “not pertaining to this office’. This issue has to be resalved
internally within the organization. Due to inter office disowning cases not
pertaining to their offices hundreds of grievances are blocked within EPFO and
are pending far even more than a year. Head office is working on this issue and
soon such cases will be sorted out office wise and sent to the correct offices.

DPG has also been requested that cases where the identification of
redressing offices is not clear such cases may be sent to HQ instead of sending to
-R.Os

It is therefore decided that

1. No office will return any case pertaining to other office. It shall follow up with
the concerned office. In such case after reference is made to the correct
office the further responsibility of delay will lie on the office to which
reference is made. :

2. While uploading replies, the name and designation of the authority
approving disposal must be mentioned in the appropriate Colum. Presently
simply APFC, RPFC it is mentioned and it is not possible to identify the
officer as such.

3. In many cases even the grievances of settlement by EPF trust have been
disowned by field offices saying that the establishment is exempted,
forgetting that even after granting exemption the EPFO remains responsible
to ensure reddressal of grievances of employees of exempted establishment.

You are, therefore, requested to note the above instructions and take care
while disposing off cases received from Cabinet Secretariat, DPG , Govt of
India.

Yours faithfully,

(Jag Mohan)

Sir,

Instructions were issued to Regional P.F. Commissioners-In-Charge of Regions

Subject: Fraudulent withdrawals from the Accounts of EPFO through fake chequesinstructions to avoid fraudulent payment- reg.

Sir,

Instructions were issued vide this office circular No. Bkg/Fraud/05/18210 dated
22/11/2011, posted at SI. No. 405 of the official website of the organization under Office Orders &
Circulars for the year 2011-12 to avoid fraudulent withdrawals.

2 References are received from various field offices pointing out that implementation of the
instructions contained in the circular referred in Para 1 above will lead to return of claims already
received in the office wherein the benefits payable are more than Rs. 10,000/-. This will lead to
undue hardship to the PF beneficiaries.

3s After examining the references received from various field offices, Head Office issued
revised instructions vide circular No. No. Bkg/Fraud/05/15614 dated 24/11/2011, posted at SI. No.
408 of the official website of the organization under Office Orders & Circulars for the year 2011-12
and thereby revised the limits of issuing cheques in Account Nos. 1,10 and 21 , only in cases
where the payments are not possible through NEFT. The said limits are as under :

i) Account No. 01 : Upto Rs. 1,00,000/-
ii) | Account No. 10 : Upto Rs. 50,000/-
iii) Account No. 21 : Upto Rs. 1,30,000/-

4. The enhanced limits resolved the problems to a great extent but field offices pointed out
following problems which still remained unresolved.

a) There is no facility provided in the Application Software for remitting
provident fund monies in death cases (Form-20) through NEFT.

b) There is no facility provided in the Application Software for remitting
provident fund monies to the Exempted Trusts through NEFT.

Page 1 of 4

c) Payment of provident fund monies(Form-19) beyond Rs. 1,00,000/-
through NEFT are not possible in the cases where the members
maintain accounts with Co-operative Banks, Regional Rural Banks and
Post Offices.

d) Pension payments going through BRS involves amount beyond the limit
of Rs. 50,000/- and there is no provision in the Application Software for
remitting the same through NEFT.

5. Earlier instructions at Para 2(v) of the circular No. Bkg/Fraud/05/18210 dated 22/11/2011
stipulate that all payments on account of Pension to other Banks, all inter-regional transfers and
transfers from EPFO to Exempted Trusts shall be made through NEFT/RTGS only. Keeping in view
the references received from the field offices and in partial modification to the instructions issued
earlier the fresh instructions are issued as under :

A.

Payment of Pension through designated Banks:

As usual the Bank Reconciliation Statements shall be generated. While generating
the forwarding letter, system will prompt to select the cheque number. The cheque
serial number so prompted by the system in sequence shall be selected and the
same shall be printed. Having printed the cheque, the same shall be cancelled. In
place of the forwarding letter so generated with cheque number by the system, a
letter of authority to the State Bank of India _ shall be prepared vide that
number(number of the cancelled cheque) with a direction to credit the amount
involved in the cheque to the account of the Pension Paying Banker by debiting
respective account of EPFO. Copy of the letter of authority shall be sent to the
designated banks alongwith BRS. The cancelled cheque and the system generated
forwarding shall be attached to the office copy of the letter of authority issued to the
State Bank of India for office record and reconciliation. Specimen of the letter of
authority to State Bank of India is enclosed herewith.

Payment to Exempted Trusts on account of transfer(Form-13) :

While generating the forwarding letter, system will prompt to select the cheque
number. The cheque serial number so prompted by the system in sequence shall be
selected and the same shail be printed. Having printed the cheque, the same shall be
cancelled. In place of the forwarding letter so generated with cheque number by the
system, an authority letter to the State Bank of India shall be prepared vide that
number(number of the cancelled cheque) with a direction to prepare Account Payee
Demand Draft/Bankers’ Cheque in the name of the Trust on account of the member
by debiting respective account of EPFO. On receipt of the Account Payee Demand
Draft/Bankers’ Cheque for the like amount (involved in the cheque),the same shall
be dispatched to the Trust with a forwarding letter and Annexure-K. The cancelled
cheque and the system generated forwarding letter shall be attached to the office
copy of the authority letter issued to the State Bank of India for office record and
reconciliation. Specimen of the letter of authority to State Bank of India is enclosed
herewith.

Sir,
Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment having reveiwed the expenditure of

various Schemes of Ministry has directed that the Autonomous Organisations under the
Ministry should monitor financial performance on monthly basis.

2. In this connection, the instructions as contained in various Circulars issued from time
to time on financial performance are reiterated. If is seen that the said instructions are not
followed in their true sprit.

3: Para 9.4, 2 of Manual of Accounting Procedure Part-l stipulates that all the offices
shall submit their Monthly Income & Expenditure Return No. Il regularly for every month by
15 of the succeeding month clearly booking expenditure to proper budget heads and
after taking into account the funds allotted under the different budget heads.

4, It is observed that the field offices are incurring expenditure over and above funds
allotted under the budget heads and send their request for ex-post facto approval. This
should be totally avoided. Similarly, if funds under a budget head are not sufficient to meet
the expenditure, ihe same is booked under a different budget head with interpretation at
their level which violates the canons of financial prudence.

3: In view of above, all the field Offices are requested to be careful while booking
expenditure to appropriate head. Unjustified interpretation while booking expenditure to a
different budget head, incuring of expenditure without sufficient funds etc. will not be
entertained on any account at Head Office.

6. Keeping all in view, the monthly Expenditure Return No.|l shall be sent to Head Office

with in the time frame in the prescribed format.

Sub: implementation of Para 10(2) of EPS, 1995 - Criteria for deciding eligibility.
Sir,
Please find enclosed herewith a copy of the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil
Appeal No. 30844/2010 alongwith copy of NCDRC order. It is observed that while disposing of
the petition, the Hon'ble Court has held that "the special leave petition is dismissed leaving
the question of law open to be decided in an appropriate case".
The matter has been examined in consultation with Panel Advocate as well as Legal
Advisor of our organization who have opined that it is not a fit case for filing review petition,
their opinion is as follows:
1.
Panel Advocate- Ms. Aparna Bhat -
"There is no point in pursuing the
review petition, as the amended section 10(2) of the EPS, 1995 has no
retrospective affect. In any event in the present case, the Hon'ble Supreme
Court while dismissing the petition was pleased to leave the
question of law open. The review petitions are decided by the same judges
in their chamber without granting any oral hearing. Therefore, there is no point in
filing the review petition against the order dated 15.11.2010."
2.
Legal Advisor- Dr. K.N. Chaturvedi-
"In view of the amendment in the actual
service weigtage of 2 years is given when a member superannuates on attaining
the age of 58 years, and who has rendered 20 years service or more. Thus, after
the amendment the age of the member at the time of superannuation must be 58
years and the number of yeas of his actual service must be 20 years or more.
Before the amendment, that is, prior of 24-07-2009 the decision of the National
Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in the case of RPFC vs Sri Mallikarjan
D. Verapur will operate depending on the facts in each case."
You are accordingly, requested to deal with legal disputes /representations where the
above judgment of NCDRC/Supreme Court is cited, on above lines.

Sub: Training Programme for Newly Promoted APFCs — Nomination(s) - Regarding.

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) has scheduled a two weeks
Training Programme for Newly Promoted APFCs from 16-25 January,2012 in its premises at -

30-31 Institutional Area, D-Block, Janak Puri, New Delhi-110058.

The course will broadly cover the following topics:

e Use management techniques for enhancing self effectiveness

¢ Describe various provisions of EPF and MP Act 1952 and its Schemes

e Initiate and conduct QJP under sections 7A and 14B of the EPF & MP, 1952 and assess the
liability.

e Explain the conditions for granting exemption

e Explain the various provisions available for Recovery of dues under the EPF and MP Act, 1952
and the IInd Schedule of the Income Tax Act.

e Explain the benefits in the EPS’ 95.

e Explain the do’s and don’ts of Conduct Rules.

e Explain the importance of CRM.

You are requested to nominate one APFC promoted from EO/AO cadre from your region including SROs
for this programme who has not undergone this training programme earlier. It may also be ensured that no
officer who is retiring in this financial year is nominated.

require specific approval of Director, NATRSS.

You are requested to relieve the officer(s) on receipt of confirmation from NATRSS with a direction to
report’to NATRSS on 16.01.2012 at 9.30 A.M. sharp.

Sir,

In pursuance to the Social Security Agreement (SSA) signed with the Republic of
Korea, the Government of India vide its letter No. Ol-11007/29/2009-EP-I] dated 30.11.2011
has now notified that the above Agreement has come into force with effect from 1% of
November, 2011. The text of the Agreement is available on the official website of EPFO,

www.epfindia.gov.in

2. The Agreement provides inter-alia for posting i.e. detachment up to a period of 60
months for employees of both the countries; therefore, the implementation process
involves the issue of “Certificate of Coverage” (COC). In view of this, concerned
employee/employer may apply for the “Certificate of Coverage” (COC) in the prescribed
format. The following instructions may be adhered to while forwarding the application for
COC to the International Workers Unit (IWU), Head Office, New Delhi :-

i. An application in the prescribed format (copy enclosed) should be filled by
both the employee and employer of an establishment covered under the Employees’
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.

ii. The application form should be accompanied by an attested copy of passport
of the applicant indicating the name, date of birth, address and other details of the
passport, such as number, date of issue, validity, etc. In case the address mentioned
in the application form differs from the address mentioned in the passport, the same
has to be certified by the employer.

iii. Each application should be properly audited for verifying correctness of the
details furnished.

Contd/-

-2iv. The application(s) complete in all respect should be forwarded to the IWU,
Head Office, New Delhi by speed post on the same day for issue of the “Certificate of
Coverage”.

V. On receipt of the Certificate of Coverage from Head Office, the employee’s
account should be flagged as “IW Account” and then the Certificate (s) handed over
to the employer.

vi. Regular compliance of the “IW Accounts” be monitored subsequently.

3. In case any further clarification is required, |\WU Head Office may be contacted.

Subject: Special Drive for recording, indexing, reviewing and weeding of
files/records from 21.11.2011 to 25.11.2011- reg.
k
As per provisions of the Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure
te•
-
cons
i
idering the urgency to reduce the volume of records being retained without
significant need for their retention, all the Sections/Office of the Ministry are
required to record/review the old files and weed out those which are no longer
civ,Atded in accordance with the applicable Records Retention Schedule.
2.
It has been expressly brought out in the Manual of Office Procedure
that Recorded files will be kept serially arranged in the sections/desks
concerned for not more than one year after which they will be transferred to
the Departmental Records Room. Further, category 'C file will be reviewed on
the expiry of the specified retention period and weeded out unless there are
sufficient grounds warranting it's further retention. Justification for retaining
a file after review will be recorded on the file with the approval of the Branch
Officer/bivisioncil Head concerned. Retention after review of a category 'C' file
will be for a period not exceeding ten years including the period already
retained. Similarly, there are provisions for handling category 'A and 'B' files. It
may be pointed out that maintenance of the recorded files is also governed by
the Public Records Act, 1993 and Public Records Rules, 1997 which are being
administered by the National Archives of India (NAI). It is important that
enough attention is paid to this aspect of O&M so as to avoid accumulation of
unwanted records, which pose problems of space and hygiene. It may also be
appreciated that above aspect of the Records Management has gained
importance with the enforcement of the "Right to Information Act, 2005"
which also puts onus on every public authority to maintain all it's records duly
catalogued and indexed in a manner and form which facilitates the right to
information under the said Act.

Sir,

Instances of encashment of fake cheques from EPF Account No. I and X have been reported
by some of the field offices. Instructions were issued earlier vide this office circular letter No.
Bkg/1(5)/2006/Bank Agreement/Part/ 27794 dated 19/09/2011 posted at SI. No. 304 of the official
website of the organization under Office Orders & Circulars issued during 2011-2012 to take
precautionary measures to avoid such fraudulent payments.

2 It is observed that inspite of instructions issued by Head Office, this problem still persists.
This matter has been examined in Head Office and following instructions are issued.

i) Immediately bank statements of EPF Account No. I & X_ be analysed and all
amounts debited therein for more than Rs. one lakh should be verified from the cash
books. This exercise should be from 1* April, 2011 onwards and if any discrepancy
is found therein, action with the Bank Authorities and to file FIR be taken wherever
required. The same should be intimated to Head Office by name to RPFC-I (F&A) by
30-11-2011.

ii) Cash Books of all the accounts should be reconciled upto date and a certificate by
the Officer-in-charge of the offices stating that cash books of all five accounts
(I,II,X,XXI and XXII) have been reconciled upto 31% October, 2011 should reach to
Head Office by name to RPFC-I(F&A) by 15-12-2011.

iii) All debits/payments made by Bank from Account No. I, X and XXI for more than
Rupees One Lakh be verified from cash books on daily basis and in case of any
variation observed, action should be taken immediately with the bank authorities and
Police Authorities wherever required.

been laid on the disposal of applications for exemption under Section 17 of the
EPF & MP Act, 1952. In this context, it is important to realize that the
applications for exemption are addressed to the appropriate government and
hence all complete applications must be placed before the same for a final
decision. Incomplete applications must hence be returned to the applicant
employer with an exhaustive list of missing documents/information and an
opportunity to submit them in a complete form.

remain pending in the offices for very long periods. Relaxation under para 79 of
the Scheme is meant only to avoid the difficulty of making an applicant
establishment comply as an unexempted establishment during the period its
exemption application is being processed and is pending a decision by the

Sub: Preparation of Internal Audit Reports — Deficiencies by IAPs — reg.
Sir,

Attention of all [APs is drawn to this office instructions regarding raising of
Audit Para pertaining to maintaining various registers in field offices. The IAPs were
required to make a single audit para in respect of the prescribed registers to be
maintained by field offices whereas some JAPs have apparently not understood the
instructions properly. Some IAPs still continue to raise separate paras for each register,
while some IAPs are including the registers in other audit observations at different areas.
Added to the confusion, some IAPs are interpreting cash books as registers; such
interpretation shows the poor knowledge they possess in the subject matter.

It is reiterated that the registers prescribed in the manual enlisted for
convenience of IAPs is already available in the net and can be easily referred to. The
IAPs shall not treat cash book as a register as it is a statutory book of accounts. The
IAPs are also directed not to update the non-maintenance of register in current audit and
recommend dropping of the same as they are not expected to update this as listed para.
This para can be only updated only on a revisional cycle after other registers have been
examined for compliance. It is suggested that they may either make a tabular listing of
register or make a bulleted listing of registers with a brief observation of not more than 3
to 4 sentences so that wastage of time on such observation is avoided.

{tis also advised that the [APs shaif prescnbe the extent of workioad based on
norms prescribed in the MAP under the subject area of each function instead of simply
writing the work norms (eg. Total claims = 10000, claims required to be verified as per
norms = 10% / 100, etc). The report shall also be made with suitable title at the
beginning of para relevant to each function like administration, compliance, accounts,
pention etc, instead of clubbing paras pertaining to different activities under one block
even though the para number may continue sequentially.

The IAPs are also informed that the paras cannot be updated where financial
loss to organisation is involved. Only normal observations of general nature of
procedural lapse without financial implications be recommended for dropping on
updation. While recommending for dropping of audit paras, the [AP must obtain a formal
reply from the Auditee Office concerned and cannot directly examine the records suomotu and recommend dropping. The above are for guidance of the [APs in case of any

Subject: Implementation of Agreement on Social Security with the Kingdom

Sir,

In pursuance of the Social Security Agreement (SSA) signed with the
Kingdom of Denmark, the Government of India has now notified vide order No. Ol11012/29/2008-EP-|I dated 24"" October, 2011 that the above Agreement has come into
effect from 1° May, 2011. The text of the Agreement is available on the official website of
EPFO, www.epfindia.gov.in.

2. The Agreement provides inter-alia for posting of employees to other
contracting states. While the period of detachment in respect of Indian employees sent
to Denmark is five years, the period in respect of Danish nationals posted to India is
three years only. In view of this concerned employee/employer may apply for the
Certificate of Coverage(COC)in the prescribed format. The following instructions may be
adhered to while forwarding the application for COC to the International Workers Unit
(IWU), Head Office, New Delhi :-

i. An application in the prescribed format (copy enclosed) should be filled by
both the employee and employer of an establishment covered under the
Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.

ii. The application form should be accompanied by an attested copy of
passport of the applicant indicating the name, date of birth, address and other
details of the passport, such as number, date of issue, validity, etc. In case the
address mentioned in the application form differs from the address mentioned in
the passport, the same has to be certified by the employer.

iii. Each application should be properly audited for verifying correctness of
the details furnished.

-2iv. The application(s) complete in all respect should be forwarded to the
IWU, Head Office, New Delhi by speed post on the same day for issue of the
“Certificate of Coverage”(COC).
V. On receipt of the Certificate of Coverage (COC) from Head Office, the
employee’s account should be flagged as “IW Account” and then the
Certificate (s) handed over to the employer.
Vi. Regular compliance of the “IW Accounts” be monitored subsequently.

3. In case any further clarification is required, IWU Head Office may be contacted.
This issues with the approval of CPFC.

period upto 31/03/2011 (u/s 17(1)(a)/para 79 or para 27A) shall be carried out by all

and submitted to their office for further necessary action.

bound manner by forming sufficient number of squads so that all the establishments are
inspected by 31.12.11. It shall be the responsibility of the officer in charge to ensure
that the inspecting teams are properly briefed and their tour programmes are approved
well in advance so that the time lines are strictly adhered.

3. It has been observed in some cases that the compliance audit reports forwarded
to Head Office are incomplete particularly where the P.F Trust of the establishment is
located outside the jurisdiction of the concerned RPFC. In such cases the officer in
charge should ensure that, either the relevant records are called for from the
establishment or a reference be sent to the concerned RPFC in whose jurisdiction the
trust is located to inspect the records of the trust and submit the required information in
a time bound manner. Under no circumstances incomplete report should be submitted
by the squad. It is also clarified that the compliance audit is to be conducted both in
respect of the establishment as well as on its P.F Trust a thorough inspection of all

relevant records should be made before recording the observations in the proforma
(Annexure-l).

Sir,

The Central Government under Section 5D[7) of the Employees’ Provident
Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 has conveyed their concurrence for
approval to the extension of the existing Productivity Linked Bonus Scheme 19982004 (Revised) for the year 2010-2011 vide their letter No. A-26022/1/94-S.S.| (Part)
dated 29.09.2011.

2. Accordingly, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner has been pleased to
approve the payment of the Productivity Linked Bonus, subject fo verification of
figures relating to workload and staff in position in each office by the Internal Audit
during next audit of Regional Office to the eligible officials of your Region as per the
Productivity Linked Bonus Scheme 1998-2004 for the year 2010-2011 for 60(Sixty)
days in all the offices of EPFO. As per the past practice the payment of bonus is to
be released well before Puja Festival to all Group ‘C’, 'D’ and Group ‘B' (NonGazetted} employees.

3. The terms and conditions governing payment of PLB will be as per the
instructions issued by the Government of India for payment of the bonus to the
employees in Central Government departments from time to time. However, the
quantum of bonus may be assessed as per the following formula circulated vide
Govt. of India, Ministry of Finance O.M. No. 14{1] E.Co-ord.|/2004 dated 30.9.2004.

= AVERAGE EMOLUMENTS X NUMBER OF DAYS OF BONUS
30.4 (AVERAGE NUMBER OF DAYS IN A MONTH)

4 The Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure has
already revised and raised the calculation ceiling to Rs. 3,500/- per month vide OM
No. 7(23}/E-III-A/2007 dated 10.10.2008. Hence, all Group C, D, and Group ‘B’ nongazetied employees are eligible for bonus. The maximum amount will, however, be
restricted to the amount admissible to those drawing emoluments of Rs.3,500/- per
month. The bonus in respect of the employees drawing emoluments of more than
Rs.3,500/- per month will be calculated as if the emoluments were Rs.3,500/- per
month.

5. The term ‘emoluments’ occurring in these orders will include Basic Pay,
Personal Pay, Special Pay, Deputation (Duty) Allowance and Dearness Allowance,
but will not include other Allowances, such as HRA, CCA Special Compensatory
(Remote locality) Allowance, Bad Climate Allowance, Children Education

Allowance and Inierim Relief etc.

Sub: New guidelines in respect of rotational transfers of officials in
the cadre of EO/AO- Regarding

Sir,

Attention of all the concerned is drawn on the above mentioned
subject. In supercession of all the existing guidelines following
guidelines are issued herewith for implementation with immediate effect:

1. Directly recruited officials on their appointment to the post of
EO/AO can only be posted as AO during the first two years.

2. Officials on their promotion to the post of EO/AO i.e. SQ/EQ can
be posted either as EO or as AO.

3. No official would function as EO in a particular area for more than
two years continuously.

4. No official would be posted as EO in any particular area for more
than four years, during his entire career.

5. No official would function as EO for more than four years
continuously. After functioning as EO for four years, an official

Contd...p/2..

-2:-

would necessarily be posted as AO. Only after working as AO for
one full year, excluding any leave availed other than Casual Leave
& Restricted Holidays, he/she may be considered for posting as
EO.

6. The power to transfer officials in the cadre of EO/AO to any station
(RO/SRO/District Head Quarter) would be vested with RPFC-I InCharge of undivided regions such as RJ, MP, BR etc. In the case
of divided regions such as MH, TN, KN, HR, UP etc. such power
would vest with ACC of the Zone.

7. The authority to allocate particular areas among EO’s and
particular task among AO’s, subject to above guidelines, would
vest with the in-charge of the Office concerned i.e. RPFC-II in the
case of SRO and RPFC-I in the case of R.O.

8. ACC(Zones) will have the authority to relax the above guidelines,
in the case of administrative exigencies or other individual
deserving cases, after recording the reasons for such relaxation in
writing.

Subject: Fraudulent payments in the Accounts of EPFO through fake chequesprecautionary measure to avoid fraudulent payment- reg.

Sir,

Instances of fraudulent encashment of cheques in EPF A/c No. I & X have been
reported by Regional Offices, Kolkata, Shimla, Jaipur, Delhi, Chandigardh and Sub-Regional
Office, Bhatinda.

The modus operandi of such fraudulent encashment are as under:

a) Cheque folios similar to those supplied to EPFO Offices by State Bank of India
have been printed with same number series.

b) The payee names have been changed.
c) The imaginary amounts have been incorporated in the cheques.

d) Cheques pertaining to transfer in/transfer out have been tampered in relation
to payee.

e) Signatures of the drawers are tampered.

The matter was taken up with State Bank of India for corrective action and with an
instruction to credit back the amount fraudulently debited from the EPF Account No.
I & X. In certain cases, the amounts have been recovered to some extent and
credited to the respective accounts.

The State Bank of India has also taken precautionary steps to overcome the
problems of fraudulent payment by putting an alert/caution message in the website

of the Bank regarding presentation of fake/forged cheques of EPFO for payment at
non-home branches.
Page 1 of 4

Instructions have been issued earlier by Finance Division vide letter No.
Bkg.1(5)2006/Agreement/Part-III/23390-23590 dated 27.10.2010(copy enclosed) to
all field offices to take all precautionary measures in this regard such as monitoring
of cash book thoroughly, especially in respect of those cheques which have been
returned back but the amount has been debited to our account by the bank against
some other cheque which may be fake cheque having same cheque number. In case
any fraudulent case is noticed, then the matter may be taken up immediately with
the bank authority and FIR should also be lodged with Police Authorities. Reports
have also been received from State Bank of India to the effect that they have also
lodged FIRs too.

It is further reiterated that all precautions shall be taken to check and arrest such
practices by fraud racket who adopt deceit practices of grabbing the Trust money
and money of the Provident Fund Members through presenting fake and tampered
cheques. The only solution to stop such practices is to transmit the claim proceeds
through National Electronic Fund Transfer(NEFT)or RTGS(Real Time Gross
Settlement) to the fullest extent.

Instructions were issued by Head Office to field offices vide letters dated
18.11.2010, 17.01.2011, 15.02.2011, 11.04.2011 and 10.08.2011 for improving the
performance. The progress on implementation of e-payment modalities has been
reviewed from time to time. It is observed that in spite of such instructions and even
after one year elapsed since e-payment modalities have been implemented in the
Organization through National Electronic Fund Transfer(NEFT), there are still some
field offices which not yet achieved the target of 70% and above in payment
through NEFT. It is very serious and it seems that the instructions have not been
followed in true spirit which resulted in fraudulent debit of money from the Trust and
cheating of Provident Fund Members by fraudulent racket. In view of above, all out
efforts are required to be taken by each office for successful implementation of epayment modalities in your office to the fullest extent.

Sub: Submission of Revised Estimates for the year 2011-12 and Budget

Estimates for the year 2012-13 proposal in respect of Employees’
Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 (including Employees’ Pension Scheme,

In accordance with the provisions c ontained in Para 58 of the EPF
Scheme 1952 on Budget, on probable Receipts and Expenditure relating to
the Administration of the Funds, the Revised Estimates for the year 2011-12 and
the Budget Estimates for the year 201 2-13 of the EPF Organisation, based on
the actual Income & Expenditure upto 30% September 2011 (i.e. from 1.4.2011
to 30.9.2011), are to be prepared and placed before the Central Board of
Trustees, for the consideration and approval in this financial year. For smooth
and timely preparation of the Revised Estimates for 2011-12 and Budget
Estimates for 2012-13, the following general instructions are issued for

guidance.

2. The budgetary exercise should not be treated as mere routine and it
should receive the personal attention of the Regional Commissioner and the
OIC of SRO both for its correctness and timely submission. On the part of the
RPFC (F&A), it should be treated as a vital function for the respective Region
including for the SROs and he should devote his personal attention in assisting
the Regional Commissioner in-charge of the Region. Efforts should be made to
frame the Revised Estimates for 20] 1-12 in such a manner that there may not
be any necessity for Re-appropriation/ Additional Funds in the last months of

the financial year.

3: The NATRSS is treated as an independent unit and separate funds are
allotted to meet iis own expendijure and the Zonal Training Institutes (ZTIs),
Sub-ZTI (Shillong) working under them. As such, Director, .NATRSS, will submit
Budget Proposal separately for NATRSS and ZIls including Sub-ZTl (Shillong).
Budget for Deputy Director, Vigilance (NZ) may be included in the proposal of
NATRSS.

4. RPFC (ASD), Head Office is also required to submit the proposal of
Revised Estimates 2011-12 & Budget Estimates 2012-13 in respect of Head
Office including the proposal of National Data Centre, NRPO, BN Enclave and
Bhavishya Nidhi Bhawan regarding requirement of funds under the budget
head "Petty Works & Maintenance of Office Building & Staff Quarters” which
will be at the disposal of Chief Engineer, PFD, Head Office.

5. Similarly, the EPF Appellate Tribunal has also been treated as a separate
Unit and separate funds are to be allotted to meet its own expenditure. As
such, Registrar, EPF Appellate Tribunal will also submit budget proposal

separately.

6. The following guidelines may please be kept in mind while formulating
the Revised Estimates 201 }-12 & Budget Estimates 20) 2-13: - .
(i) One single proposal is required to be prepared in respect of a Region as
a whole by consolidating the proposals of Regional Office and the SubRegional Offices. RPFC-in-Charge of the Region as well as RPFC-II(F&A)

may, therefore, get in touch with the OlCs of Sub-Regional Offices
under their control immediately to ensure that there is no delay in
transmission of the requisite information to their office. The Revised
Estimates 2011-12 & Budget Estimates 2012-13 for the offices of Addl.

CPFCs (Political States} and Permanent inaguiry Officers it
Parties and Deputy Directorates (Vigilance) may include their fresh

requirements, other then the routine items like Pay & allowances, TA,
Stationary, Phone, Fax bills etc. to the Regional Offices or NATRSS
whichever is concerned, where these offices are situated, which in turn,
will include the same in the consolidated budget proposal of the

Region.

ORDER - FIRST APPEAL 12 SEP ann

Appeal preferred under RTI Act, 2005 by Shri M.V. Rao referred to
Appellate Authority of PFT under EPFO Headquarter letter No.
PID/HQ/362/11 dated 08/09/2011.

Whereas Shri M.V. Rao has put up an appeal to Appellate Authority — RT|
Office of the C P.F.C., Bhikaiji Cama Place, New Delhi - 110 066 dated 21°
August 2011 with reference to his RT| Application letter dated 01.07.2011

Whereas the applicant as seeked the information for retrofitung work in
building No. 2 of EPF Staff Quarters, Borivali, Mumbai.

Whereas applicant has segregated his queries in 31 point as follows. -

(a) RT| information is required from EPFO, Head Office - point No 1 to
10.

(b) RTI information required from Addi. CPFC (MH & CG) — point No
11to20,

(C) RTI information required from RO, Bandra,— point No. 21 to 30

(d) RTI information required from all EPEO Offices of Maharashtra —
Point No. 31,

Whereas the appeal dated 21.08.2011 has given the detail that he has got no
information received for Point No. 11 to 31 confirming that he has got nothing

to say for information asked and provided for Point No. 1 to 10

And whereas in Section 6(3) of RT! Act, it has been provided that where an
application is made to public authority requesting for an information which is
held by another public authority or the subject matter of which is make more
closely connected with the functions of another public authority, the public
authority to which such application is made shall transfer the application or
such part of it as may be appropriate to that public authority and inform the
applicant immediately about such transfer, In this case the public authority
who received this application was Shri Amit Vashisht (PID) for Head Office.

Whereas on scrutiny of the information enclosed under letter dated
08/09/2011 of Shri Amit Vashisht, PID, it reveals that that CPIO of PID was
directed for responding to the portions applicable to points to be dealt by
Head Office of the application under reference i.e. Point No. 1 to 10.
Therefore, the undersigned being appellate authority to PFD only, has called
CPIO of PFD i.e. Shri Sebastian Zacharia, Assistant Engineer (Civil) and gone
into the details under the provisions of RTI Act and nomination of EPFO as
appellate authority for Head Office PFD for PFD matters and convey the
following:

(1) PID has not acted upon to go into the details of application and
referring it to respective CPIOs. An appeal is also referred wrongly
because all appeal points i.e. Point No. 11 to 31 are not meant for
Headquarter EPFO but by applicant itself have been classified for
CPIO of RO, Bandra, ACC (MH & CG) and EPFO offices at
Mumbai. Therefore, he should act as per the provisions of RT|!
correctly and take action quickly so _ that respective
CP\Os/applicable appellate authorities can function under the
provisions of RT! Act 2005 and has to dispose of the application
well within the prescribed time.

Subject: - Furnishing of details required for Assessment and timely declaration

Sir,

The work relating to the assessment of PLB for the year 2010-1] has
been taken up. The revision of PLB Scheme and approval of New Bonds
Scheme is pending with Government, and if may likely fo take some more
time for formal approval after the receipt of instructions in this regard from the
Ministry of Finance in the light of recommendations of the 6h Central Pay
Commission. Hence, It has been decided to collect the information from all
Regions relating to assessment of PLB with reference to existing the PLB
Scheme as approved by Government of India in December, 1999.
Information relating to parameters and performance as per the Scheme is to
be furnished, as usual, in the Annexure A to C (Forms enclosed).

COUN CASH

2. A time-imit of 30 days (calendar days) has been prescribed for
completing the job relating to settlement of PF, EPS and EDLI claims, Transfer
cases and cases pertaining to Advances. In case the job is not completed
within 30 days, weightage would be reduced to half for the work done
beyond 30 days. Date of receipt of claim form (complete in all respect) and
the date of dispatch of cheque would be taken into account for reckoning
30 calendar days. In some of the cases it was found that the date
mentioned on the cheque is taken into account, which is not correct. The
actual dispatch of cheque takes much more time after the cheque is
prepared and signed by the authorized officer. In order to avoid delay in
dispatch it has been decided that only the actual date of dispatch of
cheque as recorded on the slip issued by the post office should only be taken
into account. In other cases where no cheque is to be issued like PPO,
Transfer out not involving actual transfer of PF accumulations etc., the actual

date of issue of PPO and the date of actual transfer will be taken into
account.

3. As regards issue of “Annual Statement of Accounts”, it has been
classified into two groups, Viz. (1) Current year's Accounts Slips issued and (2)
Previous year’s Accounts slips issued during the current year. Accounts slips
falating to the “current Year" and those pertaining to previous years but
lssued during the current year should be shown separately. The Number of
accounts slips issued with the help of outside agencies and the number of
accounts slips prepared and issued on computers of EPFO may also please
be furnished separately in Column 9 of Annexure “A”.

4, Activity “issue of cheque against the PPO of Monthly Pension cases”
has been added in the Bonus scheme, 1999. Those beneficiaries who opt to
get Monthly Pension through their Bank Accounts are sent cheques from the
Regional/Sub-Regional Offices itself. This activity has been included in the PLB
Scheme, 1999 with a view to encourage the staff members to issue the
cheques of Monthly Pensions as promptly as possible. Accordingly,
information may be furnished separately for all the three categories as
provided in Annexure-A.

ENFORCEMENT & DAMAGES
5. The activities of “Enforcement & Damages” include:

(1) No. of 7A notices issued.
(2) No. of Speaking Orders of 7A passed and compliance effected.
(3) No. of Speaking Orders passed for Levy of Damages.
(4) No.of Recovery Certificates Executed:-
(a) For default in all the five Accounts (A/c No. 1,2,10,21 & 22)

(b) For default in 3 or 4 of the five Accounts. .
(Cc) For default in 1 or 2 of the five Accounts.
NOTICE
6. Only one notice has to be taken into account for all the three

Schemes. In case three separate notices are issued for the three Schemes, it
has to be taken as one only. Further, only the initial notice issued has to be
taken into account and not the notices issued every time after adjournment
of proceedings due to any reason. With the amendment of Section 7A, the
RPFCs are required to decide not only the quantum of dues but also to
decide the Applicability. In such cases also if more than one notices are
Issued, it should be taken as one only for the purpose of PLB return.

SPEAK ING ORDERS OF 7A PASSED AND COMPLIANCE EFFECTED

7. Against this item all the speaking orders passed under Section 7A
should not be shown. Only those orders passed, which have been complied
with, should be shown. However, instructions contained in the BIRGROING
para as “7A Notices" should also be kept in view.

Subject: Creation of a new grade of UDC (NFSG) and Stenographer Grade
‘D’ (NFSG) In CSCS and CSSS respectively.

It has been decided to create a grade of UDC ‘Non Functional
Selection Grade’ (NFSG) in Central Secretariat Clerical Services (CSCS)
cadre and Stenographer Grade ‘D’ (NFSG) in Central Secretariat
Stenographers’ Services (CSSS) Cadre in the grade pay of Rs. 4,200/- in
| Pay Band-2 with immediate effect subject to the following conditions:

(a)UDCs of CSCS and Stenographers Grade ‘D’ of CSSS shall be
eligible for placement In the Non Functional Selection Grade on
completion of 5 years of approved service as UDC/Stenographer
Grade ‘D’ subject to the condition that the total number in the
grade will be restricted to 30% of the sanctioned strength
(i.e.1104 in the grade of UDC and 385 in Steno Grade ‘D’).

(b) The officials will be placed in the Non Functional Selection Grade
as per the following procedure:

\) Department of Personnel and Training (DoP&T) will issue
a Zone of Consideration for placement of eligible officials
In NFSG as per the Common Seniority List prepared and
maintained by DoP&T in respect of UDCs of CSCS and
Stenographers Grade ‘D’ of CSSS.

ii) An internal Committee will be constituted by the Cadre
Units to review the cases of officials for placement in the
Non Functional Selection Grade and to make suitable
recommendations.

iii) The Committee. shall consider the last 5 years
ACRs/APARs of the officials. The Committee should
satisfy itself that the overall performance of the official
Is “GOOD” in the last 5 years ACRs/APARs. Such
officials would be considered suitable for placement in
the 'NFSG’.
