Subject: Compliance in respect of International Workers — regarding.

Sir,

Special Provisions pertaining to International Workers (IWs) in para 83 of the
Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 as well as para 43-A of Employees’ Pension
Scheme, 1995 have been given effect from 1° October, 2008. Subsequently, certain
amendments have also been carried out vide notification dated 11.09.2010 circulated
vide Head Office letter No. Coord/5(15)/2009/IW/07733 dated 25" /26" November, 2010.

2. In order to provide greater clarity for compliance of the statutory provisions
relating to IWs, the following instructions/clarifications are being issued for ready
reference and compliance:

(I) Coverage:

e With effect from 1 Nov. 2008 each and every International Worker (as defined in
para 83 of the EPF Scheme,1952), other than an ‘excluded employee’ is required to be
a member of the Employees’ Provident Fund.

e As on date, Social Security Agreements (SSAs) in respect of five countries have
been made effective from the date indicated against them:

Belgium 1° September, 2009
Germany 1* October, 2009
Switzerland 29" January,2011
Luxembourg 1* June, 2011

France 1* July, 2011

201

(Il) Contribution:

e The contribution in respect of all |\Ws is payable on full salary, irrespective of where
the salary is paid.

e Prior to issue of notification dated 11.9.2010, diversion of 8.33% from employer's
share of contribution to the Pension Fund was restricted to the wage ceiling of
Rs.6,500/- only. However, w.e.f. 11.09.2010, the 8.33% diversion to the Pension Fund
is calculated on full salary (i.e. not restricted to the ceiling of Rs.6,500/-).

(Ill) Compliance:
For the purpose of compliance, the first step is the identification of all I\Ws. The Ws

include Indians as well as foreigners. The Indian nationals are to be treated as IWs
w.e.f. the date of commencement of “Certificates of Coverage” issued by EPFO, Head
Office. The member will continue to be an IW till the final settlement is made in
accordance with provisions of the scheme. All foreign nationals employed in an
establishment are to be enrolled as International Workers, with the exception of those
who fall under the category of “excluded employee” on the basis of a “Certificate of
Coverage” issued by a competent agency under a SSA with India. Thus the category
of IWs has to be flagged separately for identification for the purpose of
compliance as well as settlement of their claims. A separate register in respect of
IWs may be maintained by each office.

(IV)Certificate of Coverage (COC):

e A “Certificate of Coverage” (COC) is issued in respect of an employee, who is
posted for a short term assignment by his/her Indian employer to a country with whom
India has a SSA. For this purpose, the employee is required to submit an application in
the prescribed format through his employer to the local RPFC, who in turn, after due
verification of records, forwards it to the International Workers’ Unit (IWU) at Head
Office for issue of COC.

e¢ Based on the application, the Head Office issues “COC" to the concerned RPFC for
handing over to the employer after flagging the account as IW account for monitoring
compliance in respect of contributions as per statutory provisions, as well for
disbursement of benefits.

(V) Settlement of claim in respect of IWs:
e As per notification dated 11.9.2010, an IW may withdraw, in accordance with para

83, the full amount standing to his credit in the fund in the following circumstances only:
(i) On retirement after attaining the age of 58 years

Sub: Supply of information under Right to Information Act, 2005.

Whereas Sh. Devbrat Jha has made a request in writing vide his application dated

22.07.11 for obtaining information under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

2: Whereas the undersigned having been appointed as CPIO under Section 5(1) of

the said Act is required to consider and provide the information within 30 days of the
receipt of the request.

33 And whereas Section 5(4) of the Act provides the CPIO may seek the assistance
of any other officer as he considers it necessary for the proper discharge of his duties.
Sub-section (5) further provides that any officer whose assistance has been sought shall
render all assistance to the CPIO. Once the complaint is referred “for the purposes of any
contravention of the provisions of the Act, such other officer shall be treated as CPIO”
and may be liable for penalties under Section 20 of the said Act. Further in the event of
violation of provisions / non-furnishing of documents / information such an officer is liable
for penalties under Section 20(1) of the Act @ Rs. 250/- for each day of the delay which
may extend up to Rs. 25,000/-.

4. And whereas under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act it has been provided that :
“where an application is made to a public authority requesting for an information :-
(i) which is held by another public authority, or
(ii) the subject matter of which is more closely connected with the functions of
another public authority,
the public authority, to which such application is made, shall transfer the application or
such part of it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the
applicant immediately about such transfer”.

8. Whereas on scrutiny of the application, I find that the information sought by the
applicant is closely related to and held by CPIOs of Regional Offices/Sub-Regional
Offices & CPIO/RPFC-I(ASD) Head Office, the undersigned invokes the provisions of
Section 5(4) of the said Act and transfer the application to furnish the information /

documents sought by the applicant under the RTI Act, 2005 within the prescribed time
limit directly to the applicant:

9. You may please note that any delay in furnishing the information / documents
sought for within the stipulated time limit will attract the penal provisions as provided for

Sub: Forwarding of landmark judgement delivered by Hon’ble Division Bench of
Gujarat High Court in LPA No. 12/2010 in SCA No. 3347/2009 — reg.
Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a copy of judgement dated 15/6/2011 delivered by
Hon’ble Division Bench of Gujarat High Court in the matter of EPFO Vs. Rollwell Forge Ltd.
on the issue of initiating recovery action before expiry of limitation period of appeal
prescribed under Sec.7-l| of the Act. While overturning the decision of Single Bench,
Hon’ble Division Bench has held that:

1. In the absence of any specific provision in the Act prohibiting or restraining the
authorities from taking any further action of recovery of the amount due and
payable by the employer, it is always permissible for the authorities to proceed
ahead without waiting for the expiry of the statutory time period of appeal as
provided under Section 7-I of the Act. Any other interpretation in this regard would
render provisions and the object of the Act otiose.

2. Mere filing of appeal without obtaining any relief from the Appellate authority shall
not preclude or prohibit the authorities to proceed further in the matter for recovery
of the amount.

The above judgement may be utilized for expediting recovery action and relied

upon in similar situation cases.
Yours faithfully,

1900 and Rs. 2000/-. The officials appointed in the year 1987 would get first and second
(both) financial upgradations w.e.f. 01.09.2008 since they have completed (more than) 20
years of service on 1.9.2008, the date on which the MACP came into effect.

4. Similarly, the officials wno were appointed in the year 1993, on re-training, would get
Grade Pay of Rs.1800 w.ef. 01.01.2006 and thereafter they would get first financial
upgradation i.e. Rs. 1900/- w.e.f. 01.09.2008 and second financial upgradation would be
admissible in 2013 on completion of 20 years of service.

5. The second case referred to in your aforementioned letter dated 14.12.2010 relates
to one Shri Janakiram who is visually handicapped person (blind) and appointed as Helper
on 03.07.1981 and appointed substantially to the post of helper w.e.f. 01.04.1988. He has
been doing re-canning work. Accordingly, he is performing the duties of ‘Chair Caner’ in this
organization since the date of his appointment i.e. from 03.07.1981 till date.

6. The first up-gradation under the earlier ACP Scheme was granted to Shri Janakiram
w.e.f. 01.08.1999. The official has already completed 10 years,of regular service as on
01.08.2009 in the same post and he is eligible for second upgradation under MACP
Scheme. But, the official has not been given any training (i.e., re-training to the Group D
Staff for placement in the Pay Band-1 with GP-1800/-) due to the reason that he is Visually
Handicapped. The PAC of RO, Bangalore is of the opinion that Sri Janakiram is not eligible
for upgradation under MACP Scheme.

Fe This case has also been examined. On the direction of the Head Office, the Director,
NATRSS had issued instructions vide circular No. 13(20)2007/Natrss/All ZTis/3544 dated
12.2.2009 (copy enciosed) that all Group 'D’ employees are to be trained to make them
eligible for Pay Grade revision as per the recommendations of 6" CPC. Accordingly, a
training module was designed and training was given to all Group 'D’ employees at ZTIs
keeping in mind the skill enhancing activities. Information collected from the Head Office
revealed that the Helpers(Blind Chair Caner’) of Headquarters also attended the said
training programme and the benefit of Grade Pay of Rs.1800/- was allowed to them w.e-f.
01.01.2006.

8. In the present case also, you may contact ZTI/NATRSS and Shri Janakiram may be
given training. After training, he may first be placed in the grade of Rs. 1800/- w.ef.
01.01.2006 and thereafter, he may be allowed the admissible MACP(first and second MACP
upgradations admissible on 1.9.2008, the date on which MACP came into effect and third
upgradation on completion of 30 years of service from the date of his initial regular
appointment) ignoring the promotion/ACP already given prior to 01.01.2006 in terms of
DOP&T OM No. 35034/3/2008-Estt (D) dated 16.11.2009.

Sub : Grant of MACPS benefits to EO(EQ) regarding

Sir,
Please refer to your letter No. MH/HRM-1(1)MACP-Prom/EO-A)/ 469
dated 01.12.2010 on the subject cited above.

2. It has been informed that 8 officials in the cadre of EO/AO were
promoted to the post of EO under Examination Quota directly from the feeder
cadre of UDC without being promoted as Section Supervisor. All these officals
have completed either 10 years as EO/AO or 30 years of regular service in
EPFO from the direct entry grade of LDC.

3. It has been requested to confirm whether these officials are eligible for
3 financial upgradation under MACP Scheme as recommended by the 6™ CPC
on completion of 10/30 years, as the case may be, as these officials are
already promoted to the post of EO/AO under Examination Quota which is 3
promotion in the heirarchy. Further to this, RPFC has also requested to
confirm that in case these officials are eligible for 3 financial upgradation,
whether they will be given the Grade pay of Rs. 4800/- or Rs. 5400/-.

4. The issue has been examined in the light of DoP&T OM No.
35034/3/2008-Estt.(D) dated 19.05.2009 read with clarifications issued vide
OM no. 35034/3/2008-Estt.(D) dated 09.09.2010. and in consutation with
the Internal Finance Wing. Considering the advice of Internal Finance Wing, it
has been decided that: -

(i) All those officials who have been promoted from the entry grade of
LDC to the post of UDC and subsequently promoted from UDC to the
post of EO/AAO/AO by examination and completed ten years of service
in the grade pay of EO/AAO/AO are eligible for third financial
upgradation.

P.T.O.

(ii)

oF

All those officials who have been promoted from the entry grade of
LDC to the post of UDC and subsequently promoted from UDC to the
post of EO/AAO/AO by examination and have not completed ten years
of service in the grade pay of EO/AAO/AO but completed thirty years of
service in relation to the date of joining the organisation in the entry
grade are entitled for third financial upgradation.

Provided these officials at point no. (i) and (ii) must not have availed
any ACP available prior to the implementation of MACPS.

Further, it is clarified that the aforesaid oficers on grant of MACP would

get the grade pay of Rs.4800 which is the next higher grade pay in the
hierarchy of the recommended revised pay bands and grade pay as given in
Section 1, Part -A of the first Schedule of the CCS (RP) Rules, 2008.

Yours faithfully,

Sub:- Transfer of application in terms of section 6(3) of the RTI Act,2005-regarding.
Sir,

The RTI Act casts obligation on the Public Authority to facilitate the citizens to have
access to the information held under their control and to ensure that the rights of the citizens are
met in right earnest.

Instances have been noticed where the CPJOs have returned RTI applications to the
applicants/transferring CPIOs with the reason that the information sought does not relate to their
jurisdiction.

Section 6(3) of the RTI Act specifically deals with occasions where the information
sought may not relate to the jurisdiction of the CPIO concerned. In such cases, the right approach
is to transfer the application in whole or in part, to the public authority having jurisdiction over
the subject matter on which information is sought with in the stipulated period. Returning the RTI
applications to the applicants or transferring CPIO is an incorrect practice and in contravention of
the RTI Act.

All public authorities/CPIOs are advised to take a note of this for strict compliance.

Yo ithfully

Sub: Forwarding of Judgment delivered by Hon’ble High Court of Madras
on the issue of subterfuge by splitting up of wages — regarding.

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a judgment dated 07.06.2011 of
Hon’ble High Court of Madras in connection with W.P Nos. 15823, 22480,
25442 & 25443 of 2010, 3427/2011, 19751/2010; 970,3986, 1853 and
2098 of 2011 in the matter of management of Reynolds Pens India Pvt Ltd
and other petitioners Vs. RPFC and others.

Hon’ble court has dwelt upon a common question in above petitions
that various allowances paid by the petitioners to their employees under
different heads such as Conveyance, Educational Allowances , Food
concession, Medical, Special Holidays, Night Shift Incentives, City
Compensatory Allowances etc- were amounting to wages within the
meaning of the term “Basic Wages” as per section 2(b)of the PF act
covered for deduction towards the Provident Fund.

The same may be utilised as per merits of the case, as and
when similar situation arises in field offices.

Sub:- Obligations of the Public Authorities set out in Section 4 of the RTI Act -
regarding.

Sir,

The RTI Act casts obligation on the Public Authority to faciliate the citizens to have
access to the information held under their control for ensuring the rights of the citizens of
India.

Section 4(1)(a) of RTI Act states that every public authority shall:-

“maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed in a manner and the form
which facilitates the right to information under this Act and ensure that all records that are
appropriate to be computerised are, within a reasonable time and subject to availability of
resources, computerised and connected through a network all over the country on different
systems so that access to such records is facilitated”

In the light of above mentioned section, it is requested to ensure the compliance of the
above provision under RTI Act for cataloguing records and index them for easy dissemination
and disclosure.

Sub: Time-bound updation of Members’ accounts.

Sir,

it is gathered that some of the offices are updating members' accounts by
crediting interest even though the returns like Form 3A/6A and payments position have
already been submitted by the employers. This is a serious matter and is in
contravention of the instructions issued by the Head Office vide letter No.
WSU/9(1)2011/120783 dated 29.03.2011.

respect of those establishments where single contribution had come and thereafter no
compliance is seen, in case of defaulting establishments, and those who have not
submitted returns inspite of reminders etc. even if their contributions have been

received.

3. Thus, it is reiterated that wherever returns like Form 3A/6A are received and
payment position is in order, updation of accounts Upto 2008-09 be made by taking
into account the contributions received so that the correct position is reflected.

4. Any deviation will be viewed seriously.

Sub: Augmentation of NEFT payment mode while settling claims— reg.
Sir,
You must be aware that a new dashboard from MIS point of view on claim status
data being uploaded by all field offices bas been developed and the link to same has been
given in the EPFO Website home page which could be accessed with your login ID. The
dashboard displays the total no of claims received, approved, rejected, cheque payment
made & payment made through NEFT by each office (RO/SRO) on daily, weekly,
monthly & yearly basis. It also displays if the payment NEFT data uploaded by any office
with a 'green dot' and if not with a 'red dot'. This also displays the Annual A/C work load
for last 3 years .You are requested to monitor your office by taking the help of these MIS
dashboard which is updated on a daily basis from the data dump of your office.
CPFC is personally monitoring the performance of each office displayed in the
dashboard. During a recent review meeting he has expressed his dissatisfaction on the
number of claims being settled through NEFT payment mode. On analysis of data for the
last two months, it was found that while some of the offices have not been able to utilize
this facility to its potential; few offices have approved most of the claims through NEFT.
You will observe that though the NEFT payments have improved to 61O/0 on an average
the message to the members are sent only for 41% cases. This is because the SMS is sent
only when bank gives 'R-1' report on a text format that payment has been successfully
transmitted to the destination bank branch After the successful credit of the amount in the
member bank account another report comes from the bank in `html format' as `R-2'. This
Page 1 of 2

has to be uploaded to complete the financial transaction and reconciliation of payment side
cash book. Unfortunately many offices though adopt the NEFT mode but don't liaise with
the local branch to get the `1Z-1' & `1Z-2' report, owing to which their members are l's'er
informed about their payment & they keep coming to EPFO Office & send their
grievances and the payment side cash books remain unreconciled ,
As the NEFT payment mode has been introduced with the intention of speedy
payment and easy reconciliation, such operational level delays defeat the very purpose of
the facility. You are therefore requested to pay personal attention in this regard and ensure
that there are no such difficulty in the usage of NEFT payment mode while settling claims.
If necessary, you can communicate with the banks concerned and bring out any difficulty
faced in this regard to the notice of Head Office.
All offices are requested to work towards a target of 100 % of claim settlement using
NEFT mode of payment and the other payment options like cheque and money order
should be used sparingly on need basis. The corresponding files for sending SMS should be
uploaded invariably and any difficulty in this regard should invariably be brought to the
notice of the undersigned.

With reference to the above it is informed that the Training Calendar for every year is
intimated to all concerned for having a general idea about the annual schedule and for enabling the
RPFCs to make advance planning for nominating the officers working under them according to their
needs. However, the Training Calendar is subject to modifications due to administrative or other
reasons. This may result in certain programmes getting deleted or postponed and certain
programmes getting included.

To ensure that the nomination process is smooth, NATRSS informs about the upcoming
programmes by posting communications on the website making correspondence with RPFCs
giving the exact.dates of the programmes and specifically inviting the RPFCs to make nominations in
this regard. However, it is seen that at times the RPFCs on their own relieve the officers without
consulting NATRSS depending solely on the training calendar. It is advised that henceforth RPFCs
should wait for the communication issued by NATRSS in this regard before the commencement of
every programme prior to sending nominations. This will ensure that proper planning is made by
NATRSS with regard to number of participants and taking care of their boarding lodging and other
training necessities. Once nominations are thus made, the RPFCs should relieve the officers
concerned without waiting for any confirmation from NATRSS. In case of any unavoidable problem
regarding acceptance of nomination, NATRSS would inform the RPFC accordingly.

Sir,

| would like to take this opportunity to share with you the progress
made towards computerization and increase in transparency of the
operations of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation.

2. As you are already aware all our offices have completed the
computerization process, well before the target date of March, 2011 (except
for Keonjhar, Orissa office, which could not be computerized due to lack of
office space. We are making efforts to get some space from private
individuals / state government on rent for this office).

3. | am happy to inform you that we have introduced several new features
in our system, and made it available on our website (www.epfindia.com) to
enable the members of EPFO, employers and the people at large to see the
working of the offices in all the 120 locations.

4. The claim status can now be accessed on the website, and
members who have applied for settlement of claim/transfer of account can
now see the status online from any part of the world. Earlier about a month
back we had also computerized the transfer of accounts process so that
now instead of bank drafts being sent by mail, from one Region to another,
and a separate Annexure ‘K’ by post, the amounts are transferred
electronically through NEFT and the new accounts are updated without delay.
Earlier, even when the amount was transferred in to the Regional
Commissioners account, this was not credited to the individual member
account and there was undue delay.

.2/-

-25. Another feature we have just added is the position status on-line
regarding updation of accounts in all the 120 offices of EPFO. For this
purpose, in the EPFO website, sl.no. 13 on the right, can be clicked and the
position of updation of accounts and number of accounts pending updation
can be viewed region, sub-region wise, year-wise upto the year 2008-09,
2009-10 and 2010-11 separately. Since now the system is transparent, and
the position available to anyone, it is expected that the offices who have so far
been lagging behind due to lack of monitoring, will now gear up, to update the
accounts. The employers have also been provided a software, to enable them
to download the returns and send us soft copies, so that punching of data of
members in our offices is avoided.

6. The Zonal Additional Central Commissioners and the OlCs of
regional/sub-regional offices have all been asked to ensure updation of
accounts in a mission mode (ensuring of course that settlements do not fall
beyond 30 days to the extent possible) and to monitor dealing hand wise the
progress in account updation. We have now given time to all the offices to
update the accounts upto the year 2009 -10 by June 30, 2011. We hope that
now with this systematic and transparent approach the offices will gear up for
this purpose. By fixing a reasonable target dealing hand wise, this task can
be achieved and we are making sincere efforts towards this end.

7. | just wanted to keep you informed about the developments for
increasing efficiency and transparency in the EPF offices. | hope that with the
cooperation of everyone concerned, we will be able to bring about efficiency in
our Organisation, and meet the expectations of the members and the
establishments. re

ks In order to overcome the operational problems, following steps are suggested: -

(ii) On introduction of shiff operations, one technical resource person
supported by at least another official (one of whom should be EPF staff)
should perform duties from 2.00 PM to 10.00 PM to handle the work of
second shift.

(iii) Annual accounts processing for establishments having less than 10,000
accounts should be during normal office hours as is usually done.

(iv) In respect of establishments having more than 10,000 accounts the annual
accounts should be taken up only after 4.00 PM to reduce the load on the
systems.

(v) The identification of task holders having establishments with more than
10,000 accounts should be carried out and their processing schedules
worked out. The output of each task holder should be closely monitored.

approving authorities may be required to be present during the second
shift and office orders may be issued according to the schedules finalized.

(vi) The daily routine tasks of talking backups, data dumps for transmission to
headquarters, etc. should be carried out in the second shift after the
accounts processing works have been carried out.

(vii) Each office must ensure that the information data dumps that are required
to be sent to headquarters on a daily basis are sent regularly and without
failure as they form the basis of monitoring at the central level.

Sub: - Accounting of contribution towards PF on amount of arrear and levying
damages/interest under section 14B/7Q

Sir,

An hon’ble member of CBT has raised the question of compliance in cases where wage
agreement are made enhancing wages from back dates and the arrears are paid to them on a
particular date. It has been brought to notice that some of the Offices have been taking a view that
PF contribution should have been paid on the amounts from the date they were due. For example
an agreement was made with the workers or the staff in Jan, 2010 to pay them enhanced wages
from January, 2009 and as per the terms of agreement the arrears are paid in Sept, 2010, the PF
contribution should be deducted and deposited as if the wages were paid in Sept, 2010. The view
that PF contribution should have been paid on these amounts from the date they were due (i.e. Jan,
2009 in the given example) and taking action for calculating the PF dues accordingly and levying
damages/interest under Section 14B/7Q of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 is not correct.

Accordingly, in case of arrear payments, the practice of calculating PF dues from the dates
they were due and levying damages/interest is irregular. In case the practice is in vogue in any field
Office it should be stopped.

The training calendar for Zonal Training Institute (SZ) for the year 2011-12 is enclosed. The

i.
Each newly recruited staff should be sponsored for the training programme on “Induction
Course for SSAs” within the 1st year of his/her joining the organization.

ii.
Regarding the training programme on Retirement Planning, please ensure that officials
who are due to retire within next one year and who have given notice for Voluntary

Sl.No.18 is a programme intended for Employers/EPF Members. The dates may be
circulated to the establishments under your jurisdiction on receipt of separate
communication from this end.

earmarked for each State and will be conducted at Zonal Training Institute (SZ). The
number of participants for each region in the State will be intimated separately.

v.

Zonal Training Institute (SZ) . Hence no trainees need be sponsored for this programme.

one training in two years.

sponsored again for the same training programme.

from training on their specific request.

the Zonal Training Institute (SZ) one day in advance.

Whereas Sh. S. K. Mishra has made a request in writing vide his application dated
15.4.11 for obtaining information under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

2. Whereas the undersigned having been appointed as CPIO under Section 5(1) of
the said Act is required to consider and provide the information within 30 days of the
receipt of the request.

3. And whereas Section 5(4) of the Act provides the CPIO may seek the assistance
of any other officer as he considers it necessary for the proper discharge of his duties.
Sub-section (5) further provides that any officer whose assistance has been sought shall
render all assistance to the CPIO. Once the complaint is referred “for the purposes of any
contravention of the provisions of the Act, such other officer shall be treated as CPIO”
and may be liable for penalties under Section 20 of the said Act. Further in the event of
violation of provisions / non-furnishing of documents / information such an officer is liable
for penalties under Section 20(1) of the Act @ Rs. 250/- for each day of the delay which
may extend up to Rs. 25,000/-.

4, And whereas under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act it has been provided that :
“where an application is made to a public authority requesting for an information :-
(i) which is held by another public authority, or
(ii) the subject matter of which is more closely connected with the functions of
another public authority,

the public authority, to which such application is made, shall transfer the application or
such part of it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the
applicant immediately about such transfer”.

5 Whereas on Scrutiny of the application, I find that the information sought by the
applicant is closely related to and held by CPIOs of the Regions ./ Sub-Regional
Offices, the undersigned invokes the provisions of Section 5(4) of the said Act and
transfer the application to furnish the information / documents sought by the applicant
under the RTI Act, 2005 within the prescribed time limit directly to the applicant with
confirmation to this office. You may please note that any delay in furnishing the
information / documents sought for within the stipulated time limit will attract the penal
provisions as provided for under Section 20 of the RTI Act.

6. This may please be treated as MOST URGENT.

Sub:- Clarification regarding acceptance of fees under RTI Act,2005regarding.
Sir,

Mode of payment of fee under the RTI Act,2005 has been a subject of various interpretations.
Instances have been observed where RTI applications have been returned on account of fee being made
payable to “Accounts officer’ rather than the RPFC.

2. For clarification, rule 3 of the Right to Information (Regulation of Fee and Cost) Rules,2005 is
reproduced as below:-

“3. A request for obtaining information under sub-section(1) of section 6 shall be accompanied
by an application fee of rupees ten by way of cash against proper receipt or by demand draft or bankers
cheque (or Indian Postal Order) payable to the Accounts Officer of the public authority”.

3. The Central Information Commission, while deciding appeal no. CIC/DS/A/2010/000421/SG
has also adversely noticed this practice. It is needless to emphasise that practice of rejecting RTI
applications on the ground that the fee is payable to “account officer’ is incorrect and contrary to law.

4. All the Officers discharging duties of CPIO/CAPIO are advised to adhere to fee requirements
in accordance with the RTI Act, as further clarified by the Central Information Commission,

Yours faithfully,

The undersigned is directed to say that the implementation of the
recommendations of the Sixth Central Pay Commission relating to interest
bearing advances, including House Building Advance, granted to Central
Government employees, is under consideration of the Government.
2. Pending finalisation of the new arrangements, the matter has been

are mandatory. It is seen that the meetings are not being held regularly and details of the
meetings held are not being sent to Headquarters reaularly. The matter has been raised by the
members in CBT meetings also and in the absence of the details the Headquarters is not ina
position to given convincing reply. This has been seriously viewed by the Hon'ble Minisicr for

details the latest position in respect of holding of meetings of Regional Committees, EPF for the
states is not know at the level of Headquarters. The said information is relevant to know
whether the meetings of the Regional Committee EPF are taking place regularly. Thus it is
incumbent upon Regional PF Commissioners - in Charge of the region that the quarterly returns
are sent within the stipulated time so that update and accurate information on the meetings is

Sub: _Inter-Regional transfer in the cadre of SSA.
Sir,

Dated:
To

This office is in receipt of large number of applications received from field offices requesting
Inter Region Transfer of SSAs for transfer to different regions. In this regard it is informed that there is
no provision of inter regional transfer in the cadre of SSA from one region to another as recruitment in
SSA cadre is done on regional basis based upon vacancies in the region. However, Inter Regional
transfer request are considered only on compassionate grounds depending upon facts of the case
subject to administrative exigencies, staff position/requirement in the region from where transfer is
sought and vacancy position/requirement in the region where transfer is requested.

This issue has been re-examined and to streamline the process, the requests of Inter Regional
transfers. Following guidelines are issued :

iB All requests should be carefully examined and only genuine cases should be forwarded.
Zz: All requests should be forwarded in the format as attached as Annexure “A”.
3. All requests would be considered only after official has completed 3 years of service.

Therefore, only those cases where SSA has completed 3 years of service should be
forwarded. In this regard, your attention is also invited to one of the condition mentioned in
the offer of appointment at Para 2(v) wherein it is mentioned that no application for transfer
request would be entertained before completion of 3 years from the date of joining.

4. Transfer would be made on the following terms & conditions:

(i) He/She will be accommodated as a junior most SSA in the transferred Region with
effect from the date of joining;

(ii) His/Her pay will be fixed in the cadre of SSA as per relevant rules.

(iii) The transfer being allowed at his/her own request, he/she will not be entitled to any
TA/DA and joining time.

(iv) His/Her past service rendered would not be counted for the purpose of appearing in
the departmental examination.

5. Applications received through proper channel ONLY would be considered.

6. In case any attempt is made to bring any political or other outside influence disciplinary
action as per rules would be initiated.

All request application received would normally be kept for consideration upto three years.

In case transfer request is considered, the official would be posted to the political state.
Further posting would be done by ACC (Zones) in case there is more than one Region in the
political state or by RPFC-In charge of region as the case may be.

It is therefore requested that request for inter regional transfer of SSA should be examined
as per above. The contents of this circular be brought to the notice of all concerned.

These instructions are applicable with immediate effect.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC).

Yours fajthfully,

Sub:- Recognition of All India EPF SC/ST Staff Federation — reg.
Sir,

The All India EPF SC/ST Staff Federation had been requesting for grant of recognition and
extension of other facilities at par with the general Staff Federation, on the contention that it is not a
cast specific representative body. In its support it had cited the judgement of Hon’ ble Supreme Court
in the cases of Bhaiya Lal Vs. Hari Krishan and others and State of Kerala and Others Vs. N.M.
Thomas. The matter was referred to MoL&E for looking into the matter and intimating the current
provisions / instructions of the Govt. in vogue in this regard.

MoL&E vide its letter No. Z-13018/34/2009/SS.I dated 28.03.2011 has informed that the
matter has been examined in consultation with DoP&T and has informed that as per Rule 5 (f) of the
Central Civil Services (Recognition of Service Associations) Rules, 1993, service associations which
are formed on the basis of any caste, tribe or religious denomination shall not be recognized by the
Government of India. Therefore, Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe staff/officers service association,
which are primarily formed on the basis of caste/tribe, cannot be recognized under the Central Civil
Services (Recognition of Service Associations) Rules, 1993.

434 to 437 / 2009, CAT, Ahmedabad Bench .

Sir,

The result of the EO/AO examination held from 7" to 11 December, 2009 was
announced for 25 candidates under General Category as against 26 vacancies due to
OA.No. 434 to 437/2009 of CAT, Ahmedabad bench.

The applicants in thses OAs, Anilkumar Parmar alongwith 13 others were not
eligible (as on 1.1.2009), as per recruitment rules to apply for the EO/AO Departmental
examination for promotion. However, they were allowed due to the interim orders of the
CAT. The results were not declared as the candidates were not eligible as per
recruitment rules and the decision was pending.

The said OAs are dismissed by the CAT vide its common order dated 24.02.2011. The
Hon'ble CAT has observed and ordered that;

"On examination facts of present cases, on touchstone of law relating to relaxation of
Recruitment Rules as well as order dated 22.10.2010 of Jabalpur Bench (Deepak Kulkarni & Ors.
V/s. Union of India & Ors.) we have no hesitation to hold that applicants were ineligible to appear
in the departmental examination for the post of EO/AAO. We are also of the opinion that
Tribunal cannot direct the concerned authority to relax the rules. No illegality or arbitrariness
has been pointed out as well as established in prescribing the eligibility criteria laid down under
statutory rules. Thus, finding no merits, OAs are dismissed.”

The marks of all candidates who appeared for the EO/AO Examination were given
vide letter No.Exam.5.(1)/2009/428 dated 5/13.8.2010. The following candidate comes
at the 26" position in merit order under General Category in Gujarat and is now to be
declared successful in the EO/AO Departmental competitive examination for promotion
against the examination conducted from 7 to 11™ December, 2009.

the messages are uniform for any visitor visiting either the central website of EPFO or any of
the Regional website.

Further this feature needs to be popularized among the establishments and the
employee unions so that members may take maximum advantage of the feature. The bigger
establishments may also give a link to this feature through their own websites that are
regularly visited by their employees.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: Grant of Dearness Relief to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners - Revised rate effective
from 1.1.2011.

The undersigned is directed to refer to this Department’s OM
No. 42/18/2010-P&PW(G) dated 27" September, 2010 on the subject
mentioned above and to state that the President is pleased to decide that
the Dearness Relief (DR) payable to Central Government pensioners/
family pensioners shall be enhanced from the existing rate of 45% to
51% w.e.f. 1* January, 2011.

2. These orders apply to (i) All Civilian Central Government
Pensioners/Family Pensioners (il) The Armed Forces Pensioners, Civilian
Pensioners paid out of the Defence Service Estimates, (iii) All India
Service Pensioners (iv) Raliway Pensioners and (v) The Burma Civilian
pensioners/family pensioners and pensioners/families of displaced
Government pensioners from Pakistan, who are Indian Nationals but
receiving pension on behalf of Government of Pakistan and are in receipt
of ad-hoc ex-gratia allowance of Rs, 3500/- p.m. In terms of this
Department’s OM No, 23/1/97-P&PW(B) dated 23.2.1998 read with this
Department’s OM No, 23/3/2008-P&PW(B) dated 15.9.2008.

3. Central Government Employees who had drawn lumpsum
amount on absorption in a PSU/Autonomous body and have become
eligible to restoration of 1/3 commuted portion of pension as well as
revision of the restored amount in terms of this Department's OM No.
4/59/97-P&PW (D) dated 14.07.1998 will also be entitled to the payment
of DR @ 51% w.e.f. 1.1.2011 on full pension i.e. the revised pension
which the absorbed employee would have received on the date of
restoration had he not drawn lumpsum payment on absorption and
Dearness Pension subject to fulfillment of the conditions laid down in para
5 of the O.M, dated 14.07.98. In this connection, instructions contained
in this Department’s OM No.4/29/99-P&PW (D) dated. 12.7.2000 refer,

4. Payment of DR involving a fraction of a rupee shall be
rounded off to the next higher rupee.
